intro.title: RBAC Permission Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Vue composable (hook) that checks user permissions based on a Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system. You'll learn how to encapsulate logic for determining if a user has a specific permission, such as 'edit' or 'delete', into a custom function. The core programming concept involves using Vue's Composition API, including the ref and computed functions, to create reactive state and logic. You'll implement this by defining a usePermission hook that takes a required permission and returns a computed boolean indicating whether the current user's role includes it. This approach helps keep your components clean and your permission logic centralized and maintainable.
intro.usecase: In enterprise applications like admin dashboards or SaaS platforms, RBAC permission hooks control UI visibility and functionality based on user roles. For example, a project management tool might use this hook to show 'Delete Project' buttons only to administrators, while hiding them from regular team members. Similarly, in financial software, sensitive reports or export features would be conditionally rendered based on a user's permission level. This pattern ensures secure, role-appropriate interfaces without cluttering the UI with inaccessible elements.
